headline: Town boards finalized recommendations and strategies for the October Special Town Meeting, focusing on contested CPA funding requests, zoning changes, and water infrastructure.
synopsis: In October, town boards focused heavily on warrant articles for the October 17 Special Town Meeting. The Advisory Committee recommended approving $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill to town water, but opposed Community Preservation Act funding for golf course irrigation and the Peninsula Trail footbridge due to high costs. Despite opposition from town finance leaders, the Community Preservation Committee and Trails Committee voted to keep the $428,550 trail bridge article intact on the warrant without floor amendments. The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to support a proposed zoning amendment allowing two-family dwellings, though the Advisory Committee issued an unfavorable recommendation citing density and septic concerns. In other business, the Library Trustees approved their FY28 operating budget, and the Select Board reviewed an initial study of Southborough's municipal governance structure.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail footbridge advances to Town Meeting amid cost debate
top_items.why: The Trails Committee and Community Preservation Committee decided to push forward with a $428,550 bridge proposal despite negative recommendations from finance officials.
top_items.body: Warrant Article 4 requests an additional $217,318 in Community Preservation Act funds for a 65-foot pedestrian bridge along Route 30, bringing total project costs to $428,550. Despite a 0-7 recommendation from the Advisory Committee and a 1-4 vote from the Select Board citing excessive expense, the Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to keep the article as printed rather than offering floor cuts. The Trails Committee dropped plans for a floor amendment and agreed to present the proposal as drafted with an explanatory FAQ.

top_items.title: Boards split on two-family dwelling zoning amendment
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals backed the warrant article as written, while the Advisory Committee issued an unfavorable recommendation.
top_items.body: Article 2 proposes easing restrictions on two-family dwellings by eliminating the requirement that a single-family home exist for two years before conversion. The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to support the language as drafted, concluding against last-minute revisions regarding lot sizes. However, the Advisory Committee raised concerns over septic capacity, lot impacts in Residential B zones, and property flipping, issuing an unfavorable recommendation.

top_items.title: Advisory opposes CPA funding for golf course irrigation
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee opposed using CPA funds for a $1 million irrigation system, but proponents decided to proceed with the warrant article.
top_items.body: The Southborough Golf Club is seeking funding for a $1,087,296 irrigation replacement, using $553,750 approved in 2024, $100,000 from the golf revolving fund, and over $350,000 in new CPA funds. The Advisory Committee opposed the plan, arguing that the course should be self-sustaining rather than shifting capital expenses to taxpayers. The Golf Committee approved flyer printing and voted by consensus to bring the article to Town Meeting without requesting floor amendments.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee backs $240,000 Parkerville Road water main extension
top_items.why: The committee unanimously recommended funding water service lines and a main extension for two homes affected by landfill contamination.
top_items.body: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Article 7, which authorizes $240,000 from water retained earnings. The project will extend a water main and connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill following contamination testing, with the town covering the service line connections from the street into the residences.

top_items.title: Consultant outlines review of Southborough town governance structure
top_items.why: The Select Board received an initial overview analyzing town administrator authority and municipal board structures.
top_items.body: Bill Keegan of Capital Strategic Strategies presented preliminary findings comparing Southborough's governance model, town manager powers, and committee organization against peer Massachusetts municipalities. The review comes as Special Town Meeting considers related governance articles, including converting the Town Clerk from an elected to an appointed position.

top_items.title: Library Trustees adopt FY28 operating budget
top_items.why: Trustees voted 6-0 to approve the budget while balancing state materials spending rules with rising fixed costs.
top_items.body: The Library Board of Trustees reviewed and unanimously approved the FY28 library operating budget. Board members focused on meeting the Massachusetts Board of Library Commissioners' 16 percent materials expenditure standard amid increases in fixed personnel and CW MARS network assessment costs.

top_items.title: Tricentennial Committee contracts drone show for 2027 kickoff
top_items.why: Preparations advanced for Southborough's 300th anniversary, including executing a contract for a New Year's Day drone display.
top_items.body: The Tricentennial Committee executed a contract for a 200-drone light show to open anniversary festivities on January 1, 2027, while reevaluating a proposed community bonfire. The committee also advanced coordination for a summer music festival, utility pole banners, and an antique fireman's muster with eight confirmed apparatus teams.
